text.title: Framework Major Upgrade Inventory Output Contract
text.summary: Draft-07 JSON Schema for the inventory of one major-version step: the framework and its single-major gap, the deprecation-warnings-as-errors run, every breaking change with vendor citation, reproducible call-site count, codemod or manual classification and two-axis risk score, the dependent-package compatibility table with blockers, runtime prerequisites per environment, and the review state the human checkpoint reads. Validator: `scripts/validate-framework-major-upgrade-inventory.py`.

section.title: JSON Schema (draft-07)
section.note: What the schema cannot express and the reviewer checks by hand: `target_major - current_major` is 1 and, for a multi-major path, `step_index` follows the vendor's documented order (r-fmui-one-major-step-per-inventory); `release_notes_covered` lists every minor between current and target (r-fmui-breaking-change-cited-to-vendor); `deprecation_run.ran_on_version` equals `framework.current_version` and `distinct_warnings` entries all appear in `breaking_changes` with `from_deprecation_run = true` (r-fmui-deprecation-warnings-as-errors); `risk.blast_radius` equals `call_sites.count` weighted by `runs_in` (r-fmui-risk-scored-on-two-axes); any `environments[].meets_minimum = false` implies `blocker = true` (r-fmui-runtime-prerequisites-listed); blocker entries head the risk matrix in the rendered report (r-fmui-dependent-package-compatibility).

example.note: Subject violations: a two-major jump in one inventory (r-fmui-one-major-step-per-inventory); no release notes covered and a change cited to a blog (r-fmui-breaking-change-cited-to-vendor); a plain `pytest` run with warnings not elevated and warnings without entries (r-fmui-deprecation-warnings-as-errors); status `affected` with zero call sites (r-fmui-call-site-count-per-change); `codemod` classification with no tool or dry run (r-fmui-codemod-coverage-classified); a package with no compatible release not marked blocker (r-fmui-dependent-package-compatibility); a Python prerequisite that production fails with no upgrade plan (r-fmui-runtime-prerequisites-listed); a runtime-with-no-test change with no characterisation test (r-fmui-risk-scored-on-two-axes); and an inventory self-approved by the agent that also opened the branch.

antipattern.description: `framework.major_gap` other than 1, or `step_index` out of the vendor's documented order.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-one-major-step-per-inventory: intermediate shims and codemods never apply and failures cannot be bisected.

antipattern.description: A `vendor_citation.url` that is not the vendor's release notes, upgrade guide or changelog; a minor between current and target absent from `release_notes_covered`; a suspected break listed as a change instead of under `unverified`.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-breaking-change-cited-to-vendor: the only complete list of breaks is the vendor's.

antipattern.description: `deprecation_run.command` without warnings elevated to errors, `ran_on_version` not the current version, or a distinct warning with no `breaking_changes` entry.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-deprecation-warnings-as-errors: the current version already knows most of what the next one removes.

antipattern.description: A `call_sites.count` with no `search_pattern` and `search_link`, or an entry omitted because it had zero hits instead of recorded as `not_affected`.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-call-site-count-per-change: "we probably don't use that" is how two days become three weeks.

antipattern.description: `classification = codemod` with no `codemod` block, no `dry_run_diff_lines`, or `documented_as_partial_or_experimental` true.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-codemod-coverage-classified: an experimental transform leaves 10 percent compiling and wrong.

antipattern.description: A framework-dependent package missing from `dependent_packages`, or `compatible_release_available = false` with `blocker = false` or no plan.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-dependent-package-compatibility: the unmaintained plugin is what stalls the branch on day three.

antipattern.description: `runtime_prerequisites` missing an environment, or an environment below the minimum with `blocker = false` or no `upgrade_plan`.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-runtime-prerequisites-listed: one upgrade silently becomes two in the wrong order.

antipattern.description: A `risk` without both `blast_radius` and `detectability`, or `runtime_no_test` without a linked `characterisation_test`.
antipattern.reason: r-fmui-risk-scored-on-two-axes: the budget goes where the tests are missing.

antipattern.description: `review.status = approved` with no named `reviewer` and `approved_on`, or `upgrade_branch_opened_by_agent = true`.
antipattern.reason: Human checkpoint in `03-failure-modes.xml`: opening and merging the branch are binding actions a named human approves.

text.reference: Stdlib-only validator for this contract; `--self-test` runs both examples above.
Inventory report skeleton with the same sections and field names.
